findings_and_relationships.classification: Existing current conditional aggregate API concern; no new unique count, no assumed universal API invariant or observed bad player schedule.
findings_and_relationships.detail: validate_daily_allocation checks the sum and individual 15-minute divisibility of its ten-element activity array, then independently parses two organization duration/ID tuples, without checking that each tuple matches its corresponding activity slot. DailySchedulePlan and Scheduled fields are public; ActivityMinutes::try_from accepts zero, while OrganizationAllocation::parse rejects zero with an ID and blank IDs. Direct construction or a direct mismatched helper call can therefore represent an inconsistent proposed plan if the type is intended as a complete validated aggregate.
findings_and_relationships.symbolic_case: A direct call with ten zero array entries and each separate organization tuple set to 1440 minutes with nonblank IDs meets the shown local numeric/parse conditions but yields disjoint represented durations. This is source reasoning only; it does not establish organization membership, an actual call, a saved record, or player-visible failure.
findings_and_relationships.safeguards: The inspected normal native reducer and web adapter pass the same original apprenticeship/practice values into both array slots and tuples; the native reducer builds its storage row from the plan and applies an organization membership/role guard before update. This does not prove all external or future callers safe.

findings_and_relationships.detail: parse trims a present nonempty ID and the native guard passes IDs to require_activity_membership, with practice role checked separately. The web normalize closure drops blank optional IDs before calling the same parser: a zero-minute blank becomes None in this adapter, whereas direct parse sees Some and returns OrganizationWithoutMinutes. For positive blank, web maps to missing ID and direct parse to empty ID. This is a static boundary distinction, not an automatically defective behavior: form encoding and exact identity ownership remain unresolved. effective_at operates on minute amounts and location, not organization IDs.

nonfindings.observation: DailySchedule is an explicitly broad raw transport with Default/Serde; ValidatedSchedule separately verifies numeric budget and increments, without proving organization membership. Do not assert every raw DailySchedule is invalid solely because it is unvalidated.

Redistribution transfers unavailable whole segments to available planned activities only when a positive weight exists; otherwise unavailable minutes are not reassigned, and reading is preserved. The source tests express expected behavior but no test or simulation ran.

Do any isolated writer requests satisfy all surrounding gates and persist an invalid non-quarter-hour schedule? What paths subsequently reach a saved-schedule consumer, and what is the transaction behavior? None was executed.
What are the existing organization ID owner, blank-vs-absent transport contract and actual membership/role policy across all producers?
Are all other saved-schedule writers and deserializers constrained to the private numeric validator, and should preview/native expect become structured failure?
Does the RNG weighted_index implementation provide the bounded selection contract assumed by effective_at? It was not independently read or run here.
